criterion_scores.reasoning: Step 1 (walk_artifacts' file-indexing filter) is correctly implemented — rels never carry a './' prefix, so its ignored-set comparison is format-consistent and I found no defect there. Step 2 (the reference-target exists-check in build(), line 180) is genuinely broken for './'-prefixed reference paths: the ignored set built from raw extracted paths does not match the './'-stripped `norm` used in the membership test, so a gitignored file referenced with a leading './' is computed as exists=True instead of absent. This is the exact mechanism the spec calls out as required ('ignored reference targets count as absent') and it fails on a real, anticipated input shape (the function strips './' one line earlier, so the authors clearly expected './'-prefixed paths to occur).

Both spec requirements' shells are present: pipeline-side indexing filter (a) and hub-side verifier in `pnpm check` (b), plus an extra generator-side filter as defense-in-depth. But the reference-exists layer (the mechanism most directly protecting against 'other callers of build_graph output' seeing a private path as present) has an untested edge case, and the author-reported test evidence never exercises a './'-prefixed gitignored reference — a real gap given the AC is specifically about the reference-target layer, not just the file-indexing layer.

File placement, YED-tagged comments explaining the 'why' (not just the 'what'), and the fail-closed pattern in the hub's gitIgnored() all match house convention well. One cosmetic/process nit: this diff repurposes a pre-existing helper's known-fragile path-matching pattern (already used for cosmetic 'runtime' classification) for a new privacy-critical purpose without re-validating its format invariants against the new use — that repurposing is exactly where the defect above originates.

Correctly-scoped defense-in-depth matching what the spec itself asked for (pipeline filter + hub generator filter + hub verifier), no resurrected tombstoned decisions, no fabricated numbers, no hardcoded secrets. Only a minor duplication nit (two separate gitignored()/git subprocess calls for one logical question).

Comments are generally clear about intent and the hub side fails loudly and specifically on git errors (console.error with the YED tag before process.exit(1)). But the pipeline-side comment on line 179 overclaims a guarantee ('never reaches the public graph') that this line's own logic does not actually hold in the './'-prefix case — an overstated-certainty comment sitting directly next to the defect it misdescribes, which is the diagnostics fail-anchor and also the confidence-honesty trigger.

defects.quote: +            exists = os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, norm)) and norm not in ignored
defects.why: This is the fix's core privacy mechanism ('a gitignored target counts as absent'), but `ignored` (line ~ built a few lines above from `gitignored(probe_rel)`) holds paths in whatever form the markdown prose used, while `norm` (the previous line) has ALWAYS had its leading './' stripped. `git check-ignore --stdin` echoes matches back verbatim (empirically confirmed), so a reference authored as e.g. './.claude/references/me-model.md' lands in `ignored` with the './' intact, but `norm` for that same reference is '.claude/references/me-model.md' — `norm not in ignored` is then wrongly True, so `exists` is computed as True for a private, gitignored file. This is precisely the rubric's own motivating case for the privacy_layer_defect cap, and is confirmed (not speculative): a later commit in this repo (9400825) fixes exactly this, citing a prior Sonnet judge run on this same PR. The hub's independent gitIgnored() check (which uses the same raw dst string with no stripping) still filters this specific case out downstream, but per the cap's rule a backstop does not excuse a broken first layer.

defects.quote: +            # (and the private file's existence never reaches the public graph).
defects.why: This comment asserts an absolute guarantee that this line's own logic does not actually deliver in the './'-prefix case above — the guarantee only holds because of a separate, unrelated backstop (the hub's independent filter), not because of this code. A comment stating a security property the code doesn't reliably have is the diagnostics fail-anchor ('a docstring promising a property the code doesn't have... overclaims certainty'), which the rubric says also triggers the confidence-honesty cap.

defects.quote: norm = path[2:] if path.startswith("./") else path
defects.why: This same function already special-cases './'-prefixed paths one line above the buggy check (defect above), meaning './'-prefixed references are a known, anticipated form in this exact code path — which makes it more notable that no test (automated or in the author-reported 'Test evidence' section) exercises a gitignored reference written with a leading './'. All reported test evidence (322/906/96 counts, '18 edges... exists=false', 'privacy ✓ (390 paths)') is consistent with never having hit this branch.

Minor duplication: gitignored() (a subprocess call to `git check-ignore --stdin`) is now invoked twice per build — once here on `rels` and again later in build() on `probe_rel` — for what is conceptually one 'what's ignored in this repo' question. Not a correctness issue, just an avoidable extra git subprocess round-trip.

checks_performed: Retrieved the ORIGINAL commit behind this diff (esep-cap 3f9e81e, PR #146) and its parent to see the full, unmodified functions the diff's hunks sit inside (gitignored(), walk_artifacts(), build()) — the bundle only shows changed hunks, so I needed full-file context to reason about variable formats across the two call sites.

Verified walk_artifacts()'s ignored-filter (Step 1: 'never index a gitignored file') is internally consistent: `rels` is built via os.path.relpath(), which never carries a './' prefix, so `gitignored(rels)` and `r not in ignored` compare the same string format. No bug here.

Empirically tested `git check-ignore --stdin` semantics (exit 0 = some paths matched, exit 1 = none matched; each input line is echoed back to stdout VERBATIM, './'-prefix included) to confirm the mismatch described below is real, not hypothetical.

Traced build()'s second use of the ignored set: `probe_rel` is built from raw markdown-extracted paths (whatever prefix the prose used), so `ignored = gitignored(probe_rel)` can contain './'-prefixed strings, while the membership test three lines later uses `norm` — the SAME variable this function explicitly strips './' from one line earlier (`norm = path[2:] if path.startswith('./') else path`). `norm not in ignored` therefore returns True (wrongly 'not ignored') for any reference authored with a leading './' to a gitignored target.

Confirmed this is a genuinely reachable pattern, not dead code: this exact bug was found and fixed in a LATER commit in the same repo (esep-cap 9400825, 'YED-236 judge fixes: ./-prefix normalization...'), whose message states verbatim: 'git check-ignore echoes .'/'-prefixed paths verbatim, so a reference made ONLY via './' to an existing ignored file read exists=True, class=repo' — and explicitly credits 'the build-quality judge run on PR #146 (Sonnet voting seat)' as the source. This is the rubric's own motivating case for the new privacy_layer_defect cap.
